newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions, business talks inconclusive.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions, business talks inconclusive.

text.p: Argentine business and union leaders Tuesday failed to make headway in their drive to hammer out a deal on employment and labor reforms, but agreed to continue working towards an understanding.

"We waited for 20 years to discuss working conditions (with unions)," Argentine Industrial Union (UIA) President Jorge Blanco Villegas said after three hours of talks. "We cannot expect solutions to come by in just 30 days."
CGT labor federation chairman Jorge Daer told a joint news conference with Villegas that unions were ready to continue discussing collective pay bargaining rules.

But he said the CGT was dead set against government plans to make working conditions flexible to help fight a near record 17.3 percent unemployment rate. Plans include more flexible working schedules, cutting down social benefits and replacing redundancy payouts with unemployment insurance.
"The CGT has always rejected flexibilization, which would make workers' lives more precarious," Daer said.
Villegas said the sides had agreed to put their experts to work on very complex issues. No fixed date was set for a new round of talks, although both sides made clear they would continue.
Unions last year staged three general strikes against President Carlos Menem's labor reform plans and his austerity policies.

Menem first attempted to introduce the reforms by decree, but after they were struck down by courts and frowned upon even by ruling Peronist Party legislators, he advocated business-union talks instead to solve the issue.
